confirmed.title: Restoring a backup while the logbook is still loading overwrites newer cases and reflections, even though the dialog says nothing will change
confirmed.scenario: 1. A resident signs in on a new phone, or after signing out (sign-out wipes the device copy), on weak hospital signal. 2. S.cases and S.reflections stay [] until the server's full read arrives, and the Logbook looks empty. 3. Thinking the data is lost, the resident opens More → Export / Import → Restore from backup… and picks last month's backup file. 4. The dialog says 'Add 412 cases, 30 reflections … that are missing here? … Nothing already in your logbook is changed or deleted.' 5. They tap Restore.
confirmed.consequence: Every backup case is written with a blind batch set() (cloud.saveCases) and every reflection with setDoc (cloud.saveReflection). Each server copy edited since the backup is replaced by the older backup version. A finished reflection goes back to its outline, and corrected case details and tags are undone. The write carries a fresh updatedAt, so every device takes the old copy as the newest. The write queue is bypassed, so no conflict is recorded and no copy goes to Recent changes. The newer text survives only in the history of whichever device made the edit, if it is still there. Cases deleted since the backup also come back.
confirmed.fix: In restoreBackup, wait for S.casesSynced && S.reflectionsSynced (30 s timeout with the toast 'Your logbook is still loading, try again') and use notesFromServer() for notes before working out what is missing. Better still, make the restore create-only: send each case and reflection through writes.save(kind, owner, record, null). commitRecord's transaction then refuses to replace an existing, different document (a conflict kept in Recent changes) and skips an identical one. Give downloadBackup and downloadBackupCsv the same wait.
verifier_fix:
The proposed fix is mostly right, with two changes.

1. **Work out what is missing when Restore is tapped, not when the file is read.** Today `haveCases` and `haveRefl` are fixed before `await ensureNotes()` and the dialog. Before computing them:
   - wait for `S.casesSynced && S.reflectionsSynced`, as `cloud-save.js:72` does;
   - after 30 s, refuse with "Your logbook is still loading, try again";
   - when Restore is tapped, filter again against the current `S.cases` and `S.reflections`.

   This is the minimal fix.

2. **Make the case and reflection writes create-only as a safety net.** Use `writes.save(kind, owner, r, null)`; `checkWrite` with a null base refuses a different existing document and skips an identical one. Or use a transaction that writes only when `!snap.exists()`.
   - Note that 412 separate `writes.save` transactions are slow.
   - Each edited case would also show as a "Save needs attention" conflict. Skipping documents that already exist, without raising a conflict, fits a restore that "adds what is missing" better.

The same wait in `downloadBackup` and `downloadBackupCsv` is worth adding, so a file made during loading does not hold 0 cases.

confirmed.title: Recent changes cannot restore any version of a note; for a daily note it saves both versions run together on the server
confirmed.scenario: 1. A resident's note or daily note autosaves after they delete a paragraph or overwrite a line by mistake. 2. They open More → Recent changes / Recover drafts. Every note autosave is listed there, labelled 'Reflection'. They tap 'Restore previous version' (or 'Restore this version'). 3. restore() looks the note up in S.reflections, finds nothing, and saves with base = null. commitRecord's checkWrite(current, desired, null) then always throws write-conflict while the note exists. 4. For a daily note, ui-notepad.js healDayNotes → healClosed sees that conflict and runs mergeDayNote(local = the old version, base = null, remote = the current one), which has no common base, and saves the result.
confirmed.consequence: No earlier version of a note can be restored. An ordinary note gets stuck in a conflict, and 'Restore my version' conflicts again for the same reason. Recent changes is the only place earlier note text is kept: the bin holds deleted notes only, and the summary shown is cut to 160 characters. For a daily note the server copy, synced to every device, becomes 'current text + blank line + old text', so lines are duplicated instead of restored, while the toast says the record changed elsewhere.
confirmed.fix: In restore(), take the base for notes from the notes list: `const list = job.kind === 'case' ? S.cases : job.kind === 'note' ? await notesFromServer() /* or ensureNotes() */ : S.reflections;` (import it from ui-notepad.js). Label kind 'note' as 'Note' at line 49. Add a unit test: save note v1, then v2, then restore v1 from history; the server must hold v1.
verifier_fix:
In restore(), take the base from the notes list, loading it if it isn't loaded yet:

```js
const list = job.kind === 'case' ? S.cases : job.kind === 'note' ? (await ensureNotes()) || [] : S.reflections;
```

- **Import:** ensureNotes is already exported from ui-notepad.js, which app.js imports statically.
- **Why ensureNotes:** S.notes is null until something loads the notes, and the Recovery page doesn't load them. ensureNotes returns the overlaid list, so for a conflict job it gives job.remote, the server copy. It also works offline.
- **Why not notesFromServer():** offline it blocks for up to 30 s and then throws. If it is used, catch that error and fall back to ensureNotes.
- **Order:** compute the base before writes.archive(job.key), as the code does now.
- **Label:** at line 49, label kind 'note' as 'Note' (and 'reflection' as 'Reflection').
- **Tests:** add a writes/notepad unit test. Save note v1, then v2 with base v1, then call restore with v1 and the base taken from the notes list; the server must hold v1 with no conflict job. Add a second case for a daily note: after the restore the body is v1, not v2 + v1.

confirmed.title: Moving a reflection to the recycle bin is a blind delete: an edit made on another device is lost, and that device keeps a copy that no longer exists
confirmed.scenario: 1. In the evening the resident finishes reflection R on the laptop (version V_new reaches the server). 2. Next morning the phone opens in theatre with no signal and shows its stored copy, V_old. 3. The resident moves R to the recycle bin on the phone (or a stale phone copy deletes it within seconds of an edit elsewhere). 4. Back online, the phone sends deleteDoc(reflections/R) and a bin entry whose data is V_old. 5. The laptop opens later.
confirmed.consequence: The server loses V_new with no conflict check, and the bin holds only V_old, so restoring from the bin brings back the outline instead of the finished text. On the laptop, the bin feed's tombstone carries V_old's stamp, so applyTombs keeps the newer V_new. Its delta query no longer returns R, so the laptop shows a reflection the server doesn't have until the weekly full read silently removes it. After that the finished text survives only in the laptop's own Recent changes history, if it hasn't been pushed out by later saves or wiped by a sign-out. #523 fixed exactly this for cases, but not for reflections.
confirmed.fix: Delete reflections the way notes are deleted: `writes.save('reflection', owner, { id, _deleted: true }, item)` for each entry, then watchDeletes(owner, 'reflection', ok). rollBack already handles a conflict job by keeping the newer version, with a toast. commitRecord already supports kind 'reflection' and hub.drop.
verifier_fix:
In bin.js moveToBin, the reflection branch:
- Delete through the write queue: `writes.save('reflection', owner, { id, _deleted: true }, base)`.
- Then call `watchDeletes(owner, kind, ok)`.
- `base` should be the version the device last confirmed, not always the item being binned. For the list path that is the item, or `S.reflections.find(x => x.id === id)`. For the editor path it is the editor's `session.base`: pass it in through `moveToBin(kind, item, { base })` or a per-item map, and keep the editor's `r` as the bin copy.

In rollBack, also:
1. Drop the `kind !== 'reflection' &&` guard at bin.js:106, so a reflection's conflict or failed job is archived and the conflict branch keeps the newer version with a toast.
2. Replace the blind `cloud.saveReflection(owner, { ...e.data })` at bin.js:114 with `writes.save('reflection', owner, { ...e.data }, e.data)`, as the note branch does.

Without step 1, a refused delete re-saves the stale bin copy over the newer version (checked in a scratch copy). Add an emulator or demo test: stale `S.reflections` copy, newer server version, then moveToBin. Expect the newer version kept, the bin entry removed, and no overwrite. Test the editor Delete with unsaved typing too.

confirmed.title: Backups (Drive/Dropbox, Download, notes zip) take notes from the device's possibly weeks-old stored copy, not the server
confirmed.scenario: 1. A resident writes notes and daily notes mostly on the laptop and seldom opens Notes on the phone, so the phone's stored notes are weeks old. 2. On the phone the weekly 'Your last backup was over 7 days ago' toast offers Save to Drive. The phone leaves for sign-in and comes back, and resumeCloudSave waits for the server's cases and reflections only. 3. makeBackup calls ensureNotes(), which resolves with the first list the sync engine sends: the stored copy, marked fromCache. 4. The .json.gz is uploaded, replacing today's file in Drive (PATCH; Dropbox uses mode: overwrite), and with 'Keep backups for 30 days' older files are deleted.
confirmed.consequence: The cloud backup silently leaves out every note written elsewhere since the phone last loaded notes, and holds old versions of edited ones. The toast says only 'Saved to Google Drive: 1 file', and the notes zip has the same gap. A later restore from that backup cannot bring those notes back. 'Download backup' doesn't wait for anything: on a fresh device it can save 0 cases and 0 reflections. Sync does wait for this (notesFromServer, because 'a day sent without its notes would overwrite them in the file'), but backups were not given the same wait.
confirmed.fix: In makeBackup (and makeNotesZip when used for backups) use notesFromServer() instead of ensureNotes(), and let a timeout fail the save with 'your notes didn't finish loading'. Have downloadBackup and downloadBackupCsv wait for S.casesSynced && S.reflectionsSynced as cloud-save does.
verifier_fix:
Cloud saves need the network anyway, so in filesToSave (cloud-save.js) wait for the server's notes before anything else: `await notesFromServer()`. Then makeBackup and makeNotesZip both read the synced S.notes. On a timeout, fail with the existing "your notes didn't finish loading" message. Make it a parameter, e.g. `makeBackup({ fromServer: true })`, so restoreBackup and other callers stay as they are.

Do not make Download backup and Download as one spreadsheet throw when offline: a device-copy backup made offline is still useful. Instead, wait a short time (about 10 s) for notesFromServer() and S.casesSynced && S.reflectionsSynced. If they haven't arrived, save anyway and add "(this device's copy: may miss recent changes from your other devices)" to the toast.
